name_story.story: Tariq can be understood through the Arabic form طَارِق, whose central sense is tariq; one who knocks; night visitor. Tariq is Arabic طَارِق (Ṭāriq), the active participle of طَرَقَ, meaning 'one who knocks; night visitor'.

faq.a: Tariq is associated with the Arabic form طَارِق, whose core sense is tariq; one who knocks; night visitor.

faq.q: What is the origin of Tariq?
faq.a: Tariq is associated with Arabic. Tariq is Arabic طَارِق (Ṭāriq), the active participle of طَرَقَ, meaning 'one who knocks; night visitor'.
Yes — the underlying form طَارِق is Arabic.
Tariq can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Tariq should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ط ر ق is Quranic, but Ṭāriq is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Tariq mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Tariq is rendered طارق and carries the sense طارق، رات کا آنے والا.

faq.q: What does Tariq mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Tariq is rendered طارق and carries the sense طارق، شب‌آیند.
A romanized syllable approximation is ta-riq. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Tariq?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Tariq, tariq. Script forms are طارق, طَارِق, तारिक़.

faq.q: Is Tariq a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
